title: Save and list books in the library (new books table, POST and GET /books)
summary: Users can now add a book on the Library page and see the books they saved. The API stores books in a new books table and blocks one user from saving the same ISBN twice.

beforeMerge.text: Run migrations 0042 and 0043 before the new API code goes live. Without the books table, both /books endpoints return 500.
Commit BookList.tsx and the LibraryPage.tsx change. They exist only on your machine.
Add @vitest/coverage-v8 to apps/api devDependencies, or remove --coverage from CI. Otherwise CI fails.
Optional: set BOOKS_MAX_PER_USER in production if 500 books per user is not the right limit.

sections.reason: New table and indexes. Hard to change once real data is in it.

highlights.text: New table books. One user cannot save the same ISBN twice (unique index on owner_id + isbn).
New column `authors.slug` is NOT NULL with no default. The migration fails as soon as the authors table has rows.
highlights.fix: Add `slug` as nullable, fill it for existing authors, then set NOT NULL.

highlights.text: author_id has no foreign key. Deleting an author leaves books that point to nothing.
highlights.fix: Add `REFERENCES authors(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` to `author_id`.

highlights.text: Adds the books table and an `authors.slug` column. Undo with `DROP TABLE books` and `DROP COLUMN slug`.
isbn is char(13). The API converts 10-digit ISBNs to 13 digits before saving.

files.note:
Creates the books table. Each book belongs to one user (owner_id), and deleting a user deletes their books.

Two indexes:
- **books_owner_isbn_key** blocks duplicate ISBNs per user
- **books_owner_created_idx** makes "newest first" lists fast

lineNotes.text: No foreign key. A book can point to an author that does not exist or was deleted.
Unique per user, not across all users. Two users can save the same book.

files.note: Adds a slug to authors, with a unique index. Nothing in this branch reads `slug` yet.

lineNotes.text: Blocks writes to authors while the index builds. Fine while the table is small.

highlights.fix: Keep `postgres:16` here. Move the upgrade to its own PR, with steps to dump and restore local data.

highlights.text: CI still uses postgres:16, so local and CI now run different versions.
highlights.fix: Use the same Postgres version in `docker-compose.yml` and `ci.yml`.

highlights.text: The API container gets BOOKS_MAX_PER_USER, default 500.

sections.reason: Two new API endpoints and the business rules behind them.

highlights.text:
Two new endpoints, both for logged-in users only:
- **POST /books** saves a book
- **GET /books** lists the user's books, newest first, 20 per page
Two saves at the same moment both pass the duplicate check. The database rejects one, and that user gets 500 instead of 409.
highlights.fix: In `createBook`, catch Postgres error `23505` from the insert and throw `ConflictError`, so the second save also gets 409.

highlights.text:
New API **POST /books** answers with:
- **201** and the saved book
- **400** body_invalid or isbn_invalid
- **409** book_already_saved
- **422** book_limit_reached
ISBNs are converted to 13 digits before the duplicate check, so 0441013597 and 978-0441013593 count as the same book.
errorHandler.ts did not change, but it now also returns 409 and 422. Clients that treat every error as "server down" will show the wrong message.

questions: Should the service catch the unique-index error (Postgres code 23505) and return 409?
Is 422 the right status for "limit reached", or should it be 403?

files.note:
The rules for saving a book, in this order:
1. **Check the ISBN.** It is always stored as 13 digits.
2. **Block duplicates:** same user, same ISBN.
3. **Block users over the limit:** 500 books by default.
4. **Save** the book.

lineNotes.text: Read once when the server starts. Changing the env var needs a restart.
Check, then insert. Two requests at the same moment can both pass this line. The unique index stops the second one, but as a 500 error.

files.note: Handles POST /books and GET /books. Checks the request body with zod, then calls BookService. Returns 201 with the saved book.

lineNotes.text: Thrown errors go to errorHandler (not changed), which returns 400 body_invalid.

files.note: All SQL for books. Every query filters by owner_id, so users only see their own books.
The Book type, and toBook(), which turns a database row (snake_case) into a Book object (camelCase).
Adds GET /books and POST /books. Both need a logged-in user (authGuard).

Two new error types:
- **ConflictError** returns 409
- **LimitError** returns 422

errorHandler already maps any AppError to its status code, so nothing else had to change.
